ready1_open_rewrite.title: Dataset open-ended question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The graph shows a titration curve of a weak base titrated with a strong acid. The pH was measured after small volumes of 0.075 M HCl were added to 25.0 mL of the weak base. Which arrow on the curve marks the point where the pH is equal to 14 - pK$_b$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a weak base-strong acid titration curve that decreases as the volume of HCl added increases; the horizontal axis is Volume HCl (mL), and the vertical axis is pH. Six arrows from A to F are marked on the curve. The curve has an obvious steep vertical drop near about 22 mL, which is the equivalence point region; arrow C is located at about 10–11 mL, close to half of that equivalence volume. Reasoning: When a weak base is titrated by a strong acid, at the half-equivalence point the concentrations of the weak base B and its conjugate acid BH+ are equal. At this time pH = pKa, and pKa = 14 - pKb. Therefore the position asked in the problem where pH = 14 - pKb is the half-equivalence point. In the figure, the equivalence point is about 22 mL, and the half-equivalence volume is about 11 mL, corresponding to arrow C.

method.method_draft: First describe the graph: it is a descending weak-base titration curve with labeled arrows A–F; the sharp equivalence drop is centered near 22 mL, and C is near 10–11 mL. From the text, recognize the titration is weak base plus strong acid. Use the rule that pH = 14 - pKb occurs at the half-equivalence point for this titration. Locate the equivalence volume visually at the midpoint of the steep drop, halve it, and choose the arrow at that volume. This selects arrow C.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the plotted pH decreases gradually, then sharply near about 22 mL HCl, and arrows A–F mark several positions; C is in the buffer region at roughly half of the steep-drop volume. From the text, note HCl is strong acid added to a weak base, so before equivalence moles of HCl added become moles of BH+, and remaining base is the initial base minus added HCl. Write the buffer relation for a weak base/conjugate acid pair and impose pH = 14 - pKb, giving n_BH+ = n_B. Therefore the required point is where the volume of HCl added is half the equivalence volume. Using the graph, that point is marked by arrow C.
method.CoT_raw:
Image description: The graph plots pH versus volume of HCl added in mL. The titration curve starts at high pH near 11, decreases gradually through a buffer region, then drops sharply at about 22-23 mL of HCl, and levels off at low pH. Arrows A, B, C, and D are on the gradual pre-equivalence part of the curve; C is located at roughly half the volume of the steep-drop/equivalence region. Arrows E and F are after or during the sharp drop.

Reasoning: HCl is a strong acid titrating a weak base B, so before equivalence the added HCl converts B into its conjugate acid BH+. In the buffer region, pH = pKa + log(n_B/n_BH+), and for the conjugate acid pKa = 14 - pKb. If pH = 14 - pKb, then pH = pKa, so log(n_B/n_BH+) = 0 and n_B = n_BH+. That occurs when exactly half of the original weak base has been neutralized, i.e. at half the equivalence volume. From the graph, the equivalence point is near the middle of the steep drop around 22-23 mL, so half of that volume is about 11 mL. The arrow closest to that point is C.
